name: Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo
aliases: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: National cabinet (executive branch) of the DRC; headed by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, the first woman to hold the post (appointed 1 April 2024, invested 12 June 2024; reshuffled as Suminwa II in August 2025 with 53 members). Junior executive institution to the President.

key_people.title: Vice-PM, Interior, Security, Decentralization and Customary Affairs
key_people.name: Jacquemain Shabani

key_people.title: Vice-PM, Transport and Channels of Communication
key_people.name: Jean-Pierre Bemba

key_people.title: Vice-PM, National Defense and Veterans Affairs
key_people.name: Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita

name: Présidence de la République Démocratique du Congo
aliases: President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Office of the head of state and commander-in-chief of the armed forces. Félix Tshisekedi has held the presidency since 24 January 2019 and was re-elected in the December 2023 election.

name: Parlement de la République Démocratique du Congo
aliases: Parliament of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Bicameral legislature of the DRC, comprising the Senate (upper chamber) and the National Assembly (lower chamber); the most recent parliament was inaugurated on 28 January 2019.

name: Assemblée Nationale
aliases: National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Lower house of parliament; 500 deputies elected for five-year terms. Vital Kamerhe served as its president from May 2024 until his resignation on 22 September 2025; Aimé Boji Sangara was elected his successor on 13-14 November 2025.

relationships.target_name: Parlement de la République Démocratique du Congo

name: Sénat de la République Démocratique du Congo
aliases: Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Upper house of parliament with 109 seats. Established in 1960, abolished in 1967 and re-established in 2003. Former Prime Minister Sama Lukonde has been President of the Senate since August 2024.

relationships.target_name: Parlement de la République Démocratique du Congo

name: Cour Constitutionnelle
aliases: Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Highest constitutional authority, established by the Constitution of the Third Republic on 18 February 2006; began functioning in 2015. Ensures the constitutionality of laws.

name: Cour de Cassation
aliases: Court of Cassation of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Cour suprême de la République démocratique du Congo
description: Main court of last resort of the DRC, headquartered in the Palace of Justice in Gombe, Kinshasa.

name: Commission Électorale Nationale Indépendante
description: Body responsible for organizing, supervising and overseeing elections and referendums. Initially established 29 May 2003 as the Independent Electoral Commission; restructured and renamed CENI on 3 March 2011.

name: Conseil Supérieur de l'Audiovisuel et de la Communication
aliases: Higher Council for Audiovisual and Communication
description: Independent media regulator and Institution of Support to Democracy established by Article 212 of the Constitution; replaced the High Media Authority (HAM) on 10 January 2011.

name: Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature
description: Public institution with technical and scientific mandate managing protected areas (national parks) under Ordinance-Law No. 75-023 of 22 July 1975, revised by Law No. 14/003 of 2014.

name: Ministère de l'Intérieur, Sécurité, Décentralisation et Affaires Coutumières
aliases: Ministry of the Interior and Security, Decentralization, and Customary Affairs
description: Interior and security ministry, led by a Vice-Prime Minister in the Suminwa government.

key_people.title: Vice-Prime Minister, Minister of the Interior
key_people.name: Jacquemain Shabani

name: Ministère de la Justice et Garde des Sceaux
aliases: Ministry of Justice and Keeper of the Seals (Democratic Republic of the Congo)
description: Justice ministry. Constant Mutamba held the portfolio from June 2024 until his removal on 17 June 2025; successor per the August 2025 reshuffle not confirmed in collected sources.

name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères
aliases: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Foreign affairs ministry, led by a Minister of State in the Suminwa government.

name: Ministère des Finances
aliases: Ministry of Finance of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Finance ministry of the DRC.

name: Ministère de la Défense Nationale et Anciens Combattants
aliases: Ministry of National Defense and Veterans Affairs
description: Defense ministry, led by a Vice-Prime Minister; oversees the FARDC.

key_people.title: Vice-Prime Minister, Minister of National Defense
key_people.name: Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita

name: Ministère de la Santé Publique
aliases: Ministry of Public Health (Democratic Republic of the Congo)
description: Public health ministry of the DRC.

name: Ministère des Infrastructures et Travaux Publics
aliases: Ministry of Infrastructure and Public Works
description: Infrastructure and public works ministry, led by a Minister of State.

key_people.title: Minister of State, Infrastructure and Public Works
key_people.name: Alexis Gisaro

name: Ministère des Hydrocarbures
aliases: Ministry of Hydrocarbons of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Hydrocarbons (oil and gas) ministry of the DRC.

name: Ministère des Mines
aliases: Ministry of Mines of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Mines ministry regulating the DRC's mining sector (cobalt, copper, diamonds).

name: Ministère des Transports et Voies de Communication
aliases: Ministry of Transport and Channels of Communication
description: Transport and communication routes ministry, led by a Vice-Prime Minister.

name: Ministère de la Communication et Médias
description: Communication and media ministry of the DRC.

name: Ministère de la Recherche Scientifique et Innovation
aliases: Ministry of Scientific Research and Technology
description: Scientific research and technological innovation ministry.

name: Ministère du Genre, Famille et Enfants
aliases: Ministry of Gender, Family and Children
description: Gender, family and children ministry of the DRC.

key_people.title: Minister of Gender, Family and Children
key_people.name: Léonnie Kandolo

name: Ministère des Affaires Sociales, Action Humanitaire et Solidarité Nationale
aliases: Ministry of Social Affairs, Humanitarian Action, and National Solidarity
description: Social affairs, humanitarian action and national solidarity ministry.

key_people.title: Minister of Social Action and Solidarity
key_people.name: Nathalie-Aziza Munana

name: Direction Générale de la Migration
description: Government directorate responsible for migration and border management.

name: Bureau Permanent d'Enquêtes d'Accidents et Incidents d'Aviation
aliases: Permanent Bureau of Aviation Accident and Incident Investigation
description: Aviation accident and incident investigation bureau of the DRC.

name: Assemblée Provinciale du Lomami
description: Provincial legislature of Lomami province (one of the DRC's 26 provincial assemblies); returned by the Wikidata state-institutions query for Q974.

name: La Générale des Carrières et des Mines
description: State-controlled commodity trading and mining company headquartered in Lubumbashi, successor to Union Minière du Haut-Katanga; engaged in copper and cobalt exploitation in Katanga.

name: Société Nationale d'Électricité
description: National electricity company; operates the Inga Dam facilities on the Congo River and thermal power stations. Head office in La Gombe, Kinshasa.

name: Régie de Distribution d'Eau
description: State-owned water utility responsible for producing and distributing water nationwide; established in 1929 and overseen by the Ministry of Energy and the Portfolio.

name: Société Nationale des Chemins de fer du Congo
aliases: National Railway Company of the Congo
description: National railway company operating the inland railways of the DRC.

name: Société Commerciale des Transports et des Ports
description: State-owned transport and ports operator (successor name of ONATRA, which was itself OTRACO 1960-1970 and OETC 1935-1959); operates railways, ports and Congo River barge transport. Main office on Boulevard du 30 Juin, Gombe, Kinshasa.

name: Société Minière de Bakwanga
description: State-owned diamond mining company based in Mbuji-Mayi, Kasaï-Oriental.

name: Société Aurifère du Kivu et du Maniema
description: State-owned gold (and former tin) mining company in the Kivu-Maniema region.

name: Congolaise des Hydrocarbures
description: State-owned hydrocarbons company established 9 August 1999 by governmental decree, engaged in import, export and distribution of petroleum products.

name: Congolese Posts and Telecommunications Corporation
aliases: Société congolaise des postes et télécommunications
description: State-owned postal services corporation of the DRC.

name: Congo Airways
description: State-owned flag carrier airline, based at N'djili Airport, Kinshasa; started operations on 20 October 2015. Banned from flying into the EU as of June 2026.

name: Orange RDC
description: Telecommunications operator; mobile network began operating in 2001 (originally a ZTE-Congolese state JV), fully acquired by France Télécom/Orange in 2011-2012. One of the DRC's market leaders.

name: Vodacom Congo
description: Market-leading mobile network operator in the DRC (about 21-29 million subscribers, roughly 33-38% market share), part of South Africa's Vodacom Group.

name: Airtel Congo
description: Second-largest mobile operator in the DRC (about 9.7 million subscribers, roughly 29% market share in 2025), part of Airtel Africa.

name: Africell DRC
description: Mobile network operator in the DRC (roughly 3% market share in 2025), the fourth-largest operator after Vodacom, Orange and Airtel.

name: Brasseries du Congo
description: Brewery headquartered in Limete, Kinshasa; subsidiary of Brasseries et Glacières Internationales (BGI), itself part of France's Groupe Castel. Reference brewer in the DRC since 1949.

name: Bralima
description: Major DRC brewery known for its flagship Primus lager, headquartered in Kinshasa. Part of Heineken N.V. from 1986 until April 2026, when Heineken sold its stake to Mauritius-based ELNA Holdings.

name: Compagnie Africaine d'Aviation
description: Regional airline branded flyCAA, based at N'djili Airport in Kinshasa (founded 1991 per the Wikipedia companies list).

name: Sodefor
description: Logging company operating in the DRC; subsidiary of Nordsudtimber (Liechtenstein). Subject of environmental and community-impact controversy.

name: Université de Kinshasa
description: Public university in the Lemba commune of Kinshasa; founded in 1954 as Lovanium University under Belgian colonial rule, the country's oldest and premier university (about 26,000 students).

name: Université de Lubumbashi
description: One of the largest universities in the DRC (about 33,000 students), located in Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga Province.

name: Université de Kisangani
description: Public university in Kisangani, founded in 1963 by Protestant missionaries as the Free University of the Congo; separated from the National University of Zaire in 1981.

name: Université Pédagogique Nationale
description: Public higher education institution in Ngaliema, Kinshasa dedicated to teacher training and applied pedagogy research; formerly named Institut Pédagogique National.

name: Université Catholique du Congo
description: Private Catholic university in Kinshasa, listed among the country's best universities.

name: Université Protestante du Congo
description: Private university in Kinshasa affiliated with the Church of Christ in the Congo (ECC).

name: Université Libre de Kinshasa
description: Private university in Kinshasa founded in 1988 (about 8,800 students).

name: Université Catholique de Bukavu
description: Private Catholic university in Bukavu, South Kivu, founded in 1989; member of the AUF.

name: Université Catholique du Graben
description: Private Catholic university located in Butembo, North Kivu, founded in 1989; instruction in French.

name: Université Évangélique en Afrique
description: Private interdenominational evangelical university located in Bukavu, South Kivu.

name: Université Loyola du Congo
description: Private Jesuit university in Kinshasa founded in 2016 by the Central Africa Province of the Society of Jesus.

name: Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise
description: National public broadcaster, headquartered in the RTNC Building in Lingwala, Kinshasa; operates radio and TV services nationwide (RTNC1/RTNC2 and provincial stations) in French and the four national languages. Established under a 1981 ordinance-law.

name: Radio Okapi
description: Radio network operated in partnership with MONUSCO (UN mission); one of only two outlets with national coverage. Launched 25 February 2002; broadcasts in French and Lingala, Kituba, Swahili and Tshiluba.

name: Groupe L'Avenir
description: Congolese media conglomerate comprising the daily newspaper L'Avenir, the RTG@ television channel and radio; founded by Pius Muabilu Mbayu Mukala (chairman until 2010, succeeded by his daughter Christelle Muabilu).

name: Radio Television Groupe Avenir
description: Television network of Groupe L'Avenir, one of three channels able to transmit by satellite from Kinshasa; offices in La Gombe, Kinshasa.

name: L'Avenir
description: Daily newspaper published in Kinshasa; founded in 1996 as a weekly, became a daily in 2006. Publishes in French, Lingala and Swahili; part of Groupe L'Avenir.

name: Le Potentiel
description: Congolese daily newspaper based in Kinshasa, founded in 1982 by journalist Modeste Mutinga; part of the Media 7 press group (with Radio 7 and Télé 7).

name: Actualite.cd
description: Congolese digital news website specializing in political, security and economic information; launched 4 August 2016 as part of Groupe Next Corp.

name: Top Congo FM
description: Private Kinshasa-based radio station with national coverage, one of the few outlets reaching the whole country (per RSF and the BBC media guide).

name: Digital Congo
description: Private Kinshasa-based radio and television outlet (Digital Congo FM/TV); one of three TV channels with satellite transmission from Kinshasa.

name: Radio Maendeleo
description: Community radio station in Bukavu, established in 1993 by local NGOs; one of the pioneering private radios of the liberalization era.

name: Banque Centrale du Congo
description: Central bank of the DRC, headquartered on Boulevard Colonel Tshatshi in Gombe, Kinshasa; banking regulator and issuer of the Congolese franc.

name: Rawbank
description: DRC's largest universal bank by assets (US$4.9 billion as of December 2023); created on 2 May 2002 and headquartered in Kinshasa.

name: Equity Banque Commerciale du Congo
description: Commercial bank formed by the merger of Equity Bank Congo (ex-ProCredit Bank DRC) and Banque Commerciale du Congo (heir to the 1909 Banque du Congo Belge) after Equity Group Holdings (Kenya) acquired majority shareholding in both.

name: Trust Merchant Bank
description: Commercial bank headquartered in Lubumbashi; began operations in 2004, active in retail, SME, corporate and mobile banking.

name: Ecobank RDC
aliases: Ecobank Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: DRC subsidiary of pan-African banking group Ecobank Transnational Inc. (operations in 33 African countries), licensed by the Central Bank of the Congo.

name: Standard Bank Congo
description: DRC subsidiary of Standard Bank Group, among the licensed commercial banks per the Central Bank of the Congo list.

name: United Bank for Africa DRC
description: DRC subsidiary of Nigeria's United Bank for Africa (UBA) Group.

name: Bank of Africa RDC
description: DRC subsidiary of the Bank of Africa (BOA) Group, the Moroccan-headquartered international banking group (ex-BMCE).

name: Afriland First Bank CD
description: DRC subsidiary of Cameroon's Afriland First Bank Group.

name: Access Bank RDC
description: DRC subsidiary of Nigeria's Access Bank Group.

name: FirstBank DRC
description: DRC subsidiary of Nigeria's FirstBank Group.

name: BGFIBank RDC
description: DRC subsidiary of Gabon's BGFIBank Group.

name: Solidaire Banque
description: Congolese commercial bank on the Central Bank of the Congo's licensed list (October 2023).

name: Union pour la Démocratie et le Progrès Social
aliases: Union for Democracy and Social Progress
description: Country's oldest existing party, founded 15 February 1982 under Mobutu's one-party rule; social democratic. Party of President Félix Tshisekedi and lead party of the ruling Sacred Union coalition; largest bloc in the National Assembly.

name: Parti du Peuple pour la Reconstruction et la Démocratie
aliases: People's Party for Reconstruction and Democracy
description: Political party established by former president Joseph Kabila; centre-left, social democratic. Lead party of the Common Front for Congo (FCC) coalition.

name: Mouvement de Libération du Congo
aliases: Movement for the Liberation of the Congo
description: Political party led by Jean-Pierre Bemba (Vice-PM for Transport in the Suminwa government); formerly a rebel group that fought the government during the Second Congo War, later a transitional government participant and major opposition party.

name: Ensemble pour la République
description: Political party created 18 December 2019 by businessman Moïse Katumbi (former Katanga governor); merged six member parties/groups into a single party. Liberal, centrist.

name: Engagement pour la Citoyenneté et le Développement
description: Opposition party founded in 2009 and led by its founder Martin Fayulu (2018 presidential runner-up); leads the Lamuka coalition.

name: Union pour la Nation Congolaise
description: Political party founded in 2010 by Vital Kamerhe, former Speaker of the National Assembly (2024-2025) and former Vice-PM for the Economy.

name: Avenir du Congo
description: Party of Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, former Prime Minister (2021-2024) and current President of the Senate; part of the Sacred Union coalition.

name: Mouvement Social pour le Renouveau
description: Political party founded in 2006, chaired by Pierre Lumbi; won 27 of 500 seats in the parliamentary elections of its founding era.

name: Union des Démocrates Mobutistes
description: Political party chaired by Nzanga Mobutu, son of former Zairian president Mobutu Sese Seko; founded 8 January 2007.

name: Forces du Renouveau
description: Political party originated as a breakaway faction of the rebel Rally for Congolese Democracy (RCD), still known by its original name RCD/K-ML; led by Azarias Ruberwa.

name: Union Sacrée pour la Nation
description: Ruling political coalition formed in 2020 around President Félix Tshisekedi and the UDPS; anti-Kabila big-tent platform holding a large supermajority of National Assembly seats.

name: Front Commun pour le Congo
description: Coalition formed in 2018 around former president Joseph Kabila and the PPRD; former parliamentary majority, now in opposition.

name: Lamuka
description: Opposition coalition formed in 2018 around Martin Fayulu's ECiDe; social-liberal platform.

name: Journaliste en danger
description: Independent, non-partisan non-profit founded 20 November 1998 in Kinshasa by a group of Congolese journalists for the defence and promotion of press freedom in the DRC.

name: Église du Christ au Congo
aliases: Church of Christ in the Congo
description: Umbrella association of about 100 evangelical and Protestant denominations with roughly 49 million members in the DRC; one of the country's largest civil-society actors.

name: Conférence Épiscopale Nationale du Congo
aliases: National Episcopal Conference of the Congo
Episcopal Conference of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: National assembly of Catholic bishops of the DRC; member of SECAM and the Association of Episcopal Conferences of Central Africa. Played a high-profile mediation role in the 2016-2018 political crisis.

name: Voix des Sans Voix
aliases: Voice of the Voiceless for Human Rights
description: One of the oldest Congolese human rights NGOs, operating mainly in Kinshasa with nationwide reach through the RENADHOC network of human rights NGOs.

name: Hôpital de Panzi
description: Hospital in Bukavu, South Kivu specializing in treatment of survivors of sexual violence, particularly conflict-related sexual violence; associated with Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr Denis Mukwege and the Panzi Foundation.

name: Union Nationale de la Presse Congolaise
aliases: National Union of the Congolese Press
description: Professional structure representing Congolese journalists, established during the transition alongside the media regulator and OMEC as part of the press 'refoundation' of 2004.

name: Observatoire Congolais des Médias
description: Media monitoring organization created during the transition as one of the new professional structures of the Congolese press alongside the UNPC and the CSAC.

name: African Union
description: Continental union of 55 African states including the DRC; launched 9 July 2002 in Durban (Sirte Declaration of 9 September 1999), replacing the OAU. Headquartered in Addis Ababa.

name: Southern African Development Community
description: Inter-governmental organization of 16 southern African states including the DRC, headquartered in Gaborone, Botswana; promotes regional integration, development and security cooperation.

name: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa
aliases: Marché Commun de l'Afrique Orientale et Australe
description: Regional economic community of 21 member states including the DRC, formed in December 1994; promotes free trade, customs union and common market frameworks.

name: Communauté Économique des États de l'Afrique Centrale
aliases: Economic Community of Central African States
description: African Union economic community promoting regional cooperation in Central Africa, including the DRC; founded 18 October 1983, headquartered in Libreville, Gabon.

name: Communauté Économique des Pays des Grands Lacs
aliases: Economic Community of the Great Lakes Countries
description: International organization established 20 September 1976 to promote economic integration between Burundi, the DRC and Rwanda; headquartered in Gisenyi (Rubavu), Rwanda.

name: MONUSCO
aliases: United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Mission de l'ONU pour la stabilisation en République démocratique du Congo
description: United Nations peacekeeping mission in the DRC, established 1 July 2010 (successor to MONUC); headquartered in Kinshasa. Planned withdrawal on hold amid the M23 advance in North and South Kivu.

name: Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie
description: International organization of French-speaking states and governments, including the DRC; founded 20 March 1970, headquartered in Paris.

name: Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo
aliases: Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: National military forces of the DRC; descends from the Force Publique (1885-1960) through the ANC, FAZ (Zaire era) and FAC, with the modern FARDC formed after the 2002-2003 peace process. Under the Ministry of National Defense.

relationships.target_name: Ministère de la Défense Nationale et Anciens Combattants

name: Agence Nationale de Renseignements
description: Government intelligence agency responsible for the internal and external security of the state; criticized by human rights organizations. Led by Inzun Kakiak since 2019 (per Wikipedia).

name: Police Nationale Congolaise
description: National police force of the DRC with 110,000-150,000 officers operating at provincial level under the Interior Ministry; founded 22 April 1997 and undergoing reforms.

relationships.target_name: Ministère de l'Intérieur, Sécurité, Décentralisation et Affaires Coutumières

name: Garde Républicaine
aliases: Republican Guard (Democratic Republic of the Congo)
description: Praetorian guard unit tasked with protecting the Congolese president; described by military officials as an independent branch answering to the Head of State rather than the FARDC.
